Subject: High error rates/throughput drop impacting production (urgent)

Dylan,

We started seeing a sustained throughput drop and increased 5xx errors from your hosted endpoint (redwood-prod: gptx-2048) at ~08:50 PDT this morning. Traffic for our realtime scoring pipeline is down ~45% and error rate is 6.3% for the last 25 minutes. This is directly impacting our live product.

Can you confirm if this is related to any planned maintenance or hotfix on Redwood's side? We need an ETA for mitigation and are going to stand up an incident bridge if you can join.

We're copying procurement as this is going to trigger a billing/credit conversation if SLA thresholds are exceeded.

- Samir

Subject: Internal: Nova AI production incident — need triage + compensation playbook

Team —

Nova AI (DEAL-7421) is experiencing a production-impacting throughput drop + increased 5xxs. External report attached. Initial telemetry points to elevated GPU preemptions in us-west-2 and cache thrash.

Asks:
- Rishi: can you validate if model variant rollout or kernel selector changes happened in the last 2 hours for the nova tenant pool? Also check autoscaling logs and GPU preempt count.
- Hannah: pull the per-tenant cost/loss estimate and look up their SLA (monthly availability). We need a preliminary credit calc if we miss the SLA window. Attach redwood_sla_clause.pdf for reference.
- Marissa: prep a customer-facing remediation note (draft) that includes immediate mitigations, short-term rollback options, and a good-faith credit proposal. We should avoid promising exact $ until finance approves.
- Laura: marking for visibility in case we need exec approval for larger credits or contract amendments.

We're going to stand up a bridge; I'll update with join info.

Thanks,
Dylan

Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:42:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Nova AI production incident — need triage + compensation playbook

Dylan / team —

Quick findings from initial triage:
- Around 08:47 PDT a kernel selector fallback was triggered for gptx-2048 on a subset of nodes in the nova tenant pool. The fallback path increases tokenization/attention memory overhead and reduces per-GPU concurrency.
- Autoscaler reacted but we saw a short window (08:46:50 - 08:55:30) where new pods were being unsafely scheduled leading to preemption thrash.
- No code deploys or config rollouts in the last 24 hours; the selector decision was traffic-pattern triggered.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:38 PDT:
- Forced stable kernel selector for nova tenant pool to prior profile (roll back to kernels v2.4)
- Temporarily pinned model variant to gptx-2048-v1 (pre-hotfix) for traffic coming from Nova AI's routing tag
- Increased burst capacity and disabled preemption on the pinned pool for 30 minutes

Initial outcome: error rate dropping (now 1.4%), throughput recovering (to ~92% of baseline). We'll keep the pinned config for 2 hours and then gradual release.

I'll prepare the technical write-up for the customer and attach the timeline and traces.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: novaai_traces_0801.zip)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 10:05:31 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rates/throughput drop impacting production (urgent) — remediation and next steps

Samir / Elena —

Thanks for your patience on the bridge. Summary and next steps: 

Summary:
- Root cause (preliminary): kernel-selector fallback + scheduling preemption thrash in us-west-2 for your tenant pool which temporarily reduced per-GPU throughput.
- Immediate mitigations: pinned kernels + model variant rollback + temporary preemption disable. Error rates reduced from 6.3% -> 1.4% and throughput is ~92% of normal.

Proposed remediation & compensation path:
1) Short window credit: we'll calculate an initial one-off service credit that covers the impacted time window (08:46:50 - 09:38:00 PDT). Hannah will produce a dollar estimate by end of day.
2) SLA amendment path: if you prefer a contractual amendment (e.g., dedicated capacity or explicit non-preemptible guarantees) we can route to sales/enterprise; Laura is looped for approvals.
3) Postmortem & prevention: Rishi will share a detailed timeline and proposed changes to kernel selector heuristics and scaling thresholds.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv, redwood_sla_clause.pdf

Would you like the initial credit estimate or a draft amendment first? We can do both in parallel.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
